title: Why is the sky blue (and not violet)? #shorts
description: Sunlight hits air molecules and scatters. Shorter wavelengths scatter far more (Rayleigh scattering goes as 1/wavelength^4), so blue light at ~450 nm scatters about 6 times more than red at ~700 nm. Violet scatters even more, but sunlight carries less of it and our eyes are less sensitive to it.

scenes.say: Why is the sky blue? Ten seconds.
Sunlight is every colour mixed together. When it hits the air, the tiny molecules scatter it in all directions.
But short wavelengths scatter much more. Blue light scatters about six times more than red.
So blue reaches your eyes from every part of the sky. Violet scatters even more, but sunlight has less of it, and your eyes barely notice it.

items: Violet: our eyes are less sensitive
